subject: Reading and Writing
question:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

- Ynés Mexía was a Mexican American botanist.
- Between 1917 and 1938, she collected over 150,000 botanical samples throughout the Americas.
- She collected a sample of Porophyllum ruderale in Minas Gerais, Brazil, in 1930.
- She collected a sample of Brickellia diffusa in Jalisco, Mexico, in 1926.
- Porophyllum ruderale and Brickellia diffusa are part of the Asteraceae family.
- These specimens can now be viewed online at the C.V. Starr Virtual Herbarium.

Which choice most effectively uses information from the given sentences to introduce Mexía to a new audience?
a: Many of the botanical samples collected by Ynés Mexía, such as Porophyllum ruderale and Brickellia diffusa, can now be viewed on the C.V. Starr Virtual Herbarium.
b: Botanist Ynés Mexía is known for collecting over 150,000 botanical samples throughout the Americas between 1917 and 1938.
c: Among the many botanical samples Ynés Mexía collected in Brazil in 1930 was Porophyllum ruderale of the Asteraceae family.
d: Between 1917 and 1938, Ynés Mexía collected samples of the plants Porophyllum ruderale and Brickellia diffusa, among many others, but her work was largely ignored by the scientific community during her lifetime.

subject: Reading and Writing
question:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

- Marta Danielsdottir et al.'s 2007 study of planktonic ecosystems used a nutrient–phytoplankton–zooplankton (NPZ) model.
- Diane Stoecker et al. (2017): NPZ models rely "on the differentiation of the planktonic communities into phytoplankton or zooplankton functional types," excluding mixotrophic plankton.
- Phytoplankton are exclusively phototrophic, producing nutrients via photosynthesis.
- Zooplankton are exclusively phagotrophic, obtaining nutrients by consuming other organisms.

The student wants to challenge the model used in Danielsdottir et al.'s study. Which choice most effectively uses information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
a: Since it classifies plankton as exclusively phototrophic producers or phagotrophic consumers, the model used in Danielsdottir et al.'s study may misrepresent planktonic ecosystems, in which—as Stoecker et al. note—many plankton combine these functions.
b: Danielsdottir et al.'s model disregards the respective roles of producers and consumers—organisms that, as Stoecker et al. emphasize, are essential to the trophic structure of the plankton food web.
c: By restricting plankton functional types to phytoplankton and zooplankton, the model used in Danielsdottir et al.'s study of planktonic ecosystems overlooks the many mixotrophic species that Stoecker et al. identify as being excluded from NPZ models.
d: Stoecker et al. argue that the NPZ model used in the 2007 study by Danielsdottir et al. is a common tool for studying the differentiation of phytoplankton and zooplankton functional types in various ecosystems.
